analysis: The only change in this batch is a documentation edit in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 594, base line 594). It appends one sentence to the MLX_QUANTIZED_CONSTANT_CACHE row of the GPT-OSS performance controls table: a bf16 GPT-OSS checkpoint keeps bf16 activations, so its constants need no widening and the constant cache does not apply to it. No code, default, environment variable semantics, attestation, key custody, coordinator-provider protocol, cache encryption, TTL or routing behavior changes. I checked the change against the retained threat entries for the SSD prefix cache (T-041), the provider inference engine (TB-007), and the App Attest authorization boundary (TB-011). It touches none of their controls: it does not alter the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate, the TTL, the disk budget, HMAC lookup tags, or cacheSalt scoping. The MLX_QUANTIZED_CONSTANT_CACHE row concerns an in-process BF16-to-FP32 constant reuse cache. The added text narrows its documented applicability and does not widen any security surface. Remaining question: the accuracy of the statement (that bf16 GPT-OSS checkpoints bypass the cache) is a runtime claim about libs/mlx-swift that is not supplied here, so I could not verify it. The statement is a documentation correctness question, not a security regression. The patch excerpt is marked incomplete, but the range map is complete and shows a single changed line at 594, so there are no other hidden changes in this batch.
